title: Landing Page Videos: Placement, Scripts, and Testing
summary: Learn when landing page videos help, which format to use, how to script them, and how to measure engagement and downstream conversion correctly.
body_markdown:
A landing-page video is useful when it clarifies a complex product, demonstrates an important action, supplies credible proof, or answers a purchase-blocking question. Match the video to the visitor’s intent, keep the page fast and accessible, and measure exposed visitors separately from viewers instead of treating page views as conversions.


Video is not automatically persuasive. A slow, vague autoplay loop can make a landing page worse.


## When video helps


Use video when the product is easier to understand in motion, the interface is the proof, the emotional tone matters, or the same objection appears repeatedly. Skip it when the message is already simple, the video duplicates the headline, or performance and accessibility cannot be maintained.


## Choose the right placement


Placement Best video job


Hero State promise and mechanism quickly


Product section Demonstrate the key workflow


Proof section Present an authorized customer story


FAQ Answer one complex objection


Pricing Explain fit, package, or value, not distract from comparison


## A 30-second script


1. Name the audience and valuable outcome.
2. Introduce the product and mechanism.
3. Show two or three proof beats.
4. Address the strongest objection.
5. Repeat the page’s primary action.


The ad that brought the visitor and the landing-page video should share the same promise, visual cues, offer, and next step.


## Performance and accessibility


Use a stable poster image, captions, transcript, descriptive title, visible controls, responsive sizing, and a video that does not shift the page during load. Avoid sound-on autoplay. Lazy-load carefully so the video remains discoverable in rendered HTML. Google recommends commonly used embed elements, crawlable media, and stable thumbnail URLs for video discovery.
